title: Filtered-complex boundaries lie in cycles
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $K^\bullet$ an integer-indexed cochain complex, and $F$ a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. For all $p,n,r\in\mathbb Z$, the subobjects of $\operatorname{gr}^pK^n$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] satisfy $F.\mathrm{complexBoundaries}(p,n,r)\le F.\mathrm{complexCycles}(p,n,r)$. No positivity or finiteness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 012K, displayed cycle, boundary and differential formulas and lemma-spectral-sequence-filtered-complex

proof.text: For consecutive differentials f and g, f composed with g is zero. For any subobjects S of the source and T of the target, the arrow S -> source -> middle -> target is zero and hence factors through T. Apply the pullback factorization equivalence twice, then the image/pullback adjunction: exists_f(S) <= pullback_g(T). These are Mathlib Subobject.existsPullbackAdj and Limits.pullback_factors_iff, applied directly in Lean.

Take f = d(n-1,n), g = d(n,n+1), S = F^(p-r+1)K^(n-1), T = F^(p+r)K^(n+1). Intersect the resulting inclusion with F^pK^n and add F^(p+1)K^n. Pull back along the F^p inclusion and apply the image functor of the graded projection. Functors between subobject posets preserve inequalities; the resulting sides are exactly complexBoundaries and complexCycles.
